description: ONE OF THIRTY IS NOT LIKE THE OTHER TWENTY-NINE. No mockup, no Figma, no setup, no alignment: every element is compared ONLY with its own siblings, read in one instant, so nothing here depends on the window or on matching a design layer to a DOM node — the comparison the market cannot do is the one this skips entirely. It finds the card whose padding is 12 where twenty-nine have 16, the one gap of 14 in a row of 16s, the heading left at a different line-height. FOUR SILENCERS, and each exists because without it the verb produces findings on a HEALTHY page, which is how a checker teaches its reader to ignore it: a crowd of fewer than three is not judged; values with no dominant majority mean these are different elements rather than twins with a defect; more than two differing means a deliberate second variant; and an element the page itself marks as being in another state (`aria-current`, `aria-selected`, `disabled`, a class like `is-active`) is not comparable with its siblings on appearance. That last one came from a live run that reported the SELECTED TAB as a defect — twice. `margin` and `width` are deliberately not judged: the first and last member of a list legitimately carry a different margin, and content drives width. The SPACE between members is measured instead, which carries the same information without the trap. Read `notJudged` as well as `findings`: a family that was silenced is NOT a family that passed, and every silence names its reason. Read-only and free.

selector.description: Which nodes to group into families. Default: the usual repeating kinds (li, tr, article, section, card-ish and button).

tabId.description: Target tab (from qa_tabs); omit for the active tab

within.description: Scope to this container (a CSS selector). Omit for the whole page.

title: The element that is not like its own twins
